sections.COMMENTS:
ï»¿    **COMMENTS**
The epicenter of the 1978 Gulf of Patti earthquake is located in the sea, and falls in-between the Island of Vulcano and the northern coast of Sicily. The focal mechanism solution of the main shock shows a prevalent strike-slip motion with one of the two fault planes oriented NW-SE.
The NW-SE dextral strike-slip fault of the 1978 earthquake is in agreement with the present-day stress field orientation. The focal depth of the 1978 earthquake is 10 km.
The 1978 earthquake falls on the Tindari Fault System (or Tindari-Letojanni Line), a NNW striking set of faults well documented between Mt Etna and the Aeolian Islands. The Tindari Fault System is an extensional fault system with an important right-lateral component. This system is interpreted as an ongoing accomodation zone between the adjacent contractional (to the west) and extensional crustal (to the east) sectors relative to the processes of plate convergence.
sections.OPEN QUESTIONS:
1) Is the Tindari Fault System active as a whole, or is it only its offshore portion?
2) What is the offshore pattern of this fault system?
3) Is the northern termination of the offshore Tindari Fault System well known?
4) The southern termination of the Tindari Fault System is widely debated. A master array of high-angle, NNW striking faults are located in the Tindari-Barcellona depression, for a width of about 25 km for the onshore fault system - what are its southern prolongations? Does the Tindari Fault System directly link with the Malta Escarpment?
sections.SUMMARIES:
Barbano et al. (1979)
These workers performed a macroseismic study of the 15th April 1978 earthquake.
They describe the seismic event felt for a radius of 150 km. It affected almost the whole of Sicily, and Calabria as far as the Sila plateau. The epicentre is located in the sea, and it falls in-between the Island of Vulcano and the north-east coast of Sicily. These investigators provide the epicentral coordinates and the focal depth of 25 km. They suggest a fault plane dipping 80Â° towards NE in keeping with the immersion of the fault planes of the Tindari-Giardini line.
The distribution of the aftershocks shows the greatest concentration of events near the main shock, and the strongest aftershocks are distributed along a NNW-SSE direction.
Del Pezzo and Martini (1982)
They studied the earthquake of April 15, 1978 and its aftershocks. The focal mechanism of the main shock shows a possible fault plane oriented in the NW-SE direction, but the hypocenters of the aftershocks have a scattered distribution and do not confirm the focal solution. It is possible that the station geometry could contribute to the wide scattering of the data points, masking a possible trending of the hypocenters.
Gasparini et al. (1985)
They presented a new fault-plane solution map of the Italian peninsula. The authors analised the earthquakes in the period 1905-1980, with magnitudes ranging 4-7. Their focal mechanism solution of the April 15, 1978 event in the Gulf of Patti shows a strike slip motion with one of the two fault planes aligned in the NW-SE direction.
They computed a hypocentral depth of 10 km.
Neri et al. (1996)
They used data from short-period seismic stations to investigate earthquake properties of the southern Tyrrhenian lithosphere. Their results demonstrate that in the highly stressed zone of contact between different tectonic units (Tyrrhenian and Ionian basins)
strain is released under seismic form up to depths of the order of 25 km in the crust and not just in the shallowest structures.
Billi et al. (2006)
These authors interpreted the Tindari Fault System as an ongoing accomodation zone between the adjacent contractional and extensional crustal compartments. For these authors the Tindari Fault System might be included in an incipient, oblique-extensional, transfer zone linking the ongoing contractional belts in the Calabrian-Ionian and southern Tyrrhenian compartments.
